title: AI-assisted policy templates and interactive preview flow for region/tier/fallback routing
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Summary: Build an AI-assisted policy authoring flow inside Console that helps customers construct region selection + tier routing + fallback model variant policies faster and with fewer errors. The flow combines: (1) a template gallery for common patterns (geo-primary, latency-priority, cost-optimized, hybrid), (2) an assistive constraint editor that suggests safe defaults and translations into the routing DSL, and (3) an interactive preview/simulated-run panel that shows request-level routing decisions, estimated latency/cost deltas, and safety flags before the policy is saved.

Why: Customers frequently struggle to write correct routing expressions that balance latency, cost and availability across regions and model variants. Many support requests are about accidental misconfiguration (e.g., over-constraining a route, forgetting fallback variants) or surprising cost increases when caches/batching behave differently. An assisted, preview-first authoring experience reduces onboarding friction, fewer incidents, and faster adoption of advanced routing.

What we'll deliver:
- Template gallery with 6 curated templates and an "explain this template" tooltip that uses plain-language summaries.
- AI-assist suggestion pane: given a short intent sentence (e.g., "prefer eu-west for lower latency, fallback to north-america on high load"), propose a safe routing policy + annotated translation into the Console policy DSL. Suggestions include recommended max-prefetch, batching hints, and KV cache scope.
- Live validation: linting rules that highlight incompatible constraints (region vs hardware capability, model variant mismatch) and propose fixes.
- Preview simulator: ingest a small synthetic traffic sample (from saved trace or default sample) and show per-request routing outcome heatmap, percent routed to each model variant, and estimated token-level cost/latency impact.
- Safety checks and preflight: run a lightweight safety linter and show "risk score" with recommended guardrails (e.g., add fallback, add region fallback).
- Save & rollout: allow direct conversion of a suggested policy to a canary rollout config with percentage sliders, and quick links to create a dedicated capacity reservation if template suggests it.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- The AI-assist component must be explainable: suggestions must come with a deterministic translation and highlighted heuristics so we can audit why a rule was proposed.
- Preview accuracy will be an estimate, not a guarantee. We must surface confidence intervals and avoid promising strict SLO guarantees.
- We will initially restrict assist suggestions to curated model families and supported region/hardware combos to avoid proposing unsupported pairings.

Telemetry & success metrics:
- Reduction in routing-related support tickets (target -30% in first quarter post-launch).
- % of new policies created using templates or AI-assist (target 40%).
- Median time-to-create policy in Console (target -50% for new users).
- % of saved policies that include a fallback model variant (target +25%).

Stakeholders: PM (Priya), Design (Maya Chen), Eng leads (Arjun Mehta for routing engine, Lina Gomez for console frontend), Applied ML (Zoe Park for assist safety), SRE (Kofi Mensah for preview simulator load), Customer Success (Daniel Ruiz).
acceptance_criteria: Template gallery shows 6 curated templates and persists selection to policy editor
AI-assist can accept a plain-language intent and return a proposed routing policy + annotated DSL translation
Live validation flags incompatible constraints with actionable fix suggestions
Preview simulator shows per-region and per-variant routing distribution for a sample trace and displays estimated latency and cost deltas
User can convert suggestion to a canary rollout with percentage sliders and save the policy
Confidence intervals and risk score are displayed in preview; UI never promises absolute SLOs
Telemetry events emitted for template usage, assist acceptance, preview runs, and rollout saves
